haiburden

haiburden helps public-health analysts explore published estimates of healthcare-associated infection burden in Germany and compare them with estimates for the EU/EEA.

The Shiny app answers: How do estimated infection burden and infection-type rankings differ between Germany and the EU/EEA when comparing infections, attributable deaths and healthy years lost?

Installation

Install the package from GitHub:

# Run once if remotes is not installed:
install.packages("remotes")

remotes::install_github(
  "ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-kako0004-dev"
)

Access to the Classroom repository is required if it is private.

Launch the app 

library(haiburden)
run_app()

Choose a burden measure and either the representative or convenience German sample. The table updates to show the German and EU/EEA estimates, their uncertainty limits, differences, ratios and rankings.

All displayed estimates are annual rates per 100,000 population. A ratio above 1 indicates a higher German point estimate. Rank 1 indicates the highest point estimate within that population.

Use the comparison function 

library(haiburden)

compare_burden(measure = "dalys")

compare_burden(
  measure = "infections",
  sample_id = "DE_conv"
)

difference is the German estimate minus the EU/EEA estimate. ratio is the German estimate divided by the EU/EEA estimate. Uncertainty limits describe the original estimates, not the calculated differences or ratios.

Included data

  • hai_germany: 30 records from Table 1 containing German annual totals for infections, attributable deaths, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years of life lost (YLLs), and years lived with disability (YLDs).
  • hai_comparison: 54 records from Table 2 containing annual rates per 100,000 population for infections, attributable deaths and DALYs across three survey samples.

The five infection types are healthcare-associated pneumonia, urinary tract infection, primary bloodstream infection, surgical-site infection and Clostridioides difficile infection.

Access the dataset and function documentation with:

?hai_germany
?hai_comparison
?compare_burden
?run_app

Data source and preparation

Source: Zacher et al. (2019), Application of a new methodology and R package reveals a high burden of healthcare-associated infections (HAI) in Germany compared to the average in the European Union/European Economic Area, 2011 to 2012.

https://doi.org/10.2807/1560-7917.ES.2019.24.46.1900135

Values and 95% uncertainty intervals were manually transcribed from Tables 1 and 2, rearranged into long format, and supplemented with descriptive labels and source information.

The preparation script downloads a reference copy of the article, imports the transcribed values, checks the data structure and uncertainty limits, and saves the packaged datasets.

To recreate the datasets, run this from the repository root with usethis installed:

source("data-raw/hai-burden.R")

This reproduces preparation of the published estimates; it does not rerun the authors’ statistical model.

Interpretation and limitations

  • These are historical, model-based estimates, based on German survey data from 2011 and EU/EEA survey data from 2011–2012.
  • They do not describe current hospital conditions.
  • The German representative and convenience samples are alternative estimates and must not be combined.
  • The EU/EEA comparison is pooled, rather than individual-country data.
  • Differences and rankings of point estimates do not establish statistical significance.
  • The “All” category covers only the five infection types studied. It must not be added to the individual infection estimates.
  • Sums of individual medians need not equal published overall medians.
